name: Macro Decode
description: Decodes complex economic systems and modern financial anxieties through data-driven forensics and premium visual explanations. Tone of an investigative journalist: skeptical of hype, heavily data-reliant, slightly contrarian. Positions itself as the Truth-Teller revealing the hidden mechanics of the economy.
_sourceOfTruthNote: This file is UI/catalog presentation metadata only (read by channelRegistryService.buildCreativeDNA for the /api/channels response). It is NOT what drives actual episode production. Production behavior (narration_style, image_style, animation_style, voice ID, etc.) is owned by the channel_dna DB table, populated by migrations/007_macro_decode_rename.js, and read at render time via config-reader.cjs. Keep this file's creativeDNA in sync with that migration by eye, but do not treat it as authoritative — see macro-decode-channel-dna-v2.md for the real source brief.

creativeDNA.tone: analytical, skeptical, contrarian, data-driven — investigative journalist validating macro-anxiety, then explaining the real mechanism with hard data
creativeDNA.storyStructure: Curiosity Loop + Problem Stack: contrarian hook (0-15s) -> context (15-60s) -> the common understanding (1-4m) -> what's actually happening, the turn (4-7m) -> why it matters for you (7-10m) -> conclusion / open loop (10-12m)
creativeDNA.hookFormula: Pattern Interrupt — bold contrarian claim + specific value promise, e.g. "The index-fund advice you have heard is mostly right. But three specific cases break it."
creativeDNA.visualStyle: deep navy blue, gold/amber, white — clean, geometric, professional. Motion graphics mandatory: charts build dynamically, numbers count up. Static graphs are never used.
creativeDNA.narrationStyle: crisp, confident, analytical, direct-address ("you"), data-heavy but conversational — not calm/soft, not documentary-cinematic
creativeDNA.differentiation: Explains the rules of the game (economics/finance), not people breaking the rules — no boardroom villains or rise-and-fall arcs like corporate-scandal channels. Never generic budgeting advice. If a claim can't be backed by a chart, a statistic, or an established economic principle, it doesn't belong on this channel.
